visualReview.notes: Current fountain exterior reviewed in 51 portable, shared-material and medium-fi views. Deep coffered niche, giant columns, Oceanus and flanking figures, distinct horses/tritons, papal crest, rough travertine ledges, stepped spillways, mapped basin and dry stairs remain readable. Poses and carving are faceted interpretations; full Palazzo Poli, inscriptions, precise anatomy and unseen surfaces remain outside the approved scope.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Current shared-material renders inspected. Existing architectural graphs retained; no new texture or atlas. No visible UV/material regression. Capture verifies eviction and ground restoration; bounded source-ground preview remains the geographic scope.

mediumFiReview.notes: All 25 current medium-fi views inspected, including four actual LOD transitions, detail cameras, silhouette, noon/late lighting and economy/high settings. Synthetic context does not establish live map placement. Street sculpture reductions and close-up caps retain the main forms.

geographicReview.notes: Mapped Palazzo Poli facade width49.6916m and heading0.337308rad, whole-site component0 and separate actual water polygon used. Aggregate water multipolygon contains other Rome fountains; those components explicitly excluded. Exterior dry Piazza path at local[-5.7253,31.4338] controls ground contact; runtime terrainReference derived from its native coordinate. Immutable original Terrarium field covers256m; no data flattening/fitting. Immediate4.2m backing facade only: full palace body preserved, replacement disabled. Provider samples may oversample native DEM and do not constitute surveyed architectural elevations.

runtimeLodReview.notes: Strict 1000/4000/16000/64000 triangle ceilings met. Detailed source master retained separately. Street anatomy uses position-welded static sculpture reductions (8cm human-space bound, 4cm horse-space bound; Trevi human scale at most1.26). Close-up cap permits removal of fine components within its declared 4cm NYSE/6cm Trevi reduction setting. Error figures are reducer settings, not surveyed global accuracy.

scope: Half-metre sampled physical coverage and specific rays prove these controls, not complete manifold topology or walkable interior/collision.
Native map width and basin traces are quantized controls; sculpture/ornament and vertical levels remain photo interpretations. Actual visual and geographic reviews are separate.

validation.sourceHeightPolicy: Original provider heights retained; public physical-ground controller modifies only rendered mesh while model visible.

limitations: Native map geometry is quantized and low-zoom; precise sculpted rock placement and facade heights are photographic interpretations, not a construction survey.
Native whole-fountain envelope differs from actual water edge. Preserve both; do not fill the whole envelope with water.
Mapped Palazzo Poli has rear courts and wings; asset scope covers fountain facade and immediate backing thickness, not complete palace or its interior.
Statues, arms, horses, shell chariot and papal crest must retain interpreted recognizable silhouettes; no exact facial/inscription/art-conservation reproduction.
Native map preparation establishes location and signed axes; geometry, independent terrain and actual visual/placement acceptance must be separately verified before any completion annotation.

Facade width49.69m follows mapped line;26.3m reported overall height is a non-survey visual control. Individual cornices, column dimensions, water/step levels, rock positions and statue poses are photographic estimates. Sculptures retain restrained silhouettes, not exact faces, muscle/finger/fabric detail or copied reliefs/inscriptions.

Immediate4.2m backing facade is a bounded wall volume, not the complete Palazzo Poli. No interior, water simulation, fountain plumbing or navigable collision claim. Waterfall strips are static pale geometric surfaces.

Original Terrarium pixels may oversample much coarser composite source data;1m sampling does not imply survey accuracy. Provider-relative vertical reference only; default coarse host terrain compatibility not certified.

Fine sculpture and rock surfaces are conservative faceted interpretations from photographs, not a sculptural survey or exact replica. Water is an opaque static surface; no real fluid simulation or submerged bathymetry.
Bounded immediate Palazzo Poli fountain facade only; full palace and neighboring city remain separate supporting context.

imageryReview.notes: The cleared RoyFokker night exterior confirms the central giant arch, paired columns, lateral statue niches and layered rocky water basins. Current pale architectural composition and simplified statues preserve the recognizable hierarchy. Side palace fabric, anatomy, rock detail and precise hydraulic elements remain approximate; night lighting is not baked into materials. Exact published Qualla paths, metadata, public-domain/CC0 attribution and bytes agree. No supplemental imagery was needed.
